newsitem.title: USA: Glimcher in development plan with Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Glimcher in development plan with Nomura.

text.p: Glimcher Realty Trust said on Wednesday it received a commitment from a U.S. affiliate of Nomura Securities Co Ltd for up to $1 billion in financing to fund development of new shopping centers.

Glimcher, a real estate investment trust (REIT), said the first phase of the financing calls for Nomura Asset Capital Corp to provide $135 million in equity financing for three projects underway in Kansas City, Elizabeth, New Jersey and Carson, California.

Projects developed as a result of the partnership will be owned jointly by Glimcher, Nomura, and the Glazier's Pension Fund, which is responsible for pre-development tasks such as acquiring sites and obtaining entitlements and permits.
"It makes a wonderful situation because (the Glaziers) get the jobs and we don't have to put up any front money," Glimcher said.
Ownership of mall developments will go 40 percent to Nomura and 30 percent each to Glimcher and the pension fund, Glimcher Realty chairman Herbert Glimcher said.

Glimcher executives said they were unable to offer a revised earnings outlook for the REIT based on the ongoing projects and the Nomura pact. They did say the financing agreement would allow the company to grow much more rapidly.
"This will give us the most significant growth we have had," said Glimcher.
Development of the New Jersey and California malls, each of which are 1.8 million square foot projects, rank as Glimcher's largest. The company is already reviewing several new sites for development.
"We have another three or four sites in the pipeline," said president David Glimcher.
The Kansas City mall is expected to open in the second half of 1997, and the company expects a stabilized financial impact from the mall to start by the end of 1998.
The New Jersey mall is slated to open in late 1998 and the California site in 1999.
